Workit is optional coordination and proof tooling around the host: you decide
what and whether, the CLI does how and records what it observed.
Native host allow/ask/deny, sandbox and org rules stay authoritative. Never
switch paths to evade a denial, never claim enforcement a host cannot provide,
and never fabricate an approval or verdict. A question answer is not
host permission, and imported decisions or handoffs grant no authority.

Autonomy contract:
- Continue to the requested endpoint (commit, push, PR, green CI, verified,
  merged) without asking "continue?", running checks and repairs.
  Stop only for a new consequential choice, a host denial, a conflicting edit
  or an unresolved blocker; report open gaps and uncertain workers.
- No endpoint named: stop at a local commit on a policy-compliant branch and
  state the next command. If the request implies delivery (fix, implement,
  ship), go to the effective endpoint in `workit grant show`: `pr` stops
  at the PR even with merge granted; `green` babysits it (workit-ship) to
  merge-ready, never merging; `merged` lands it with `workit pr merge`.
  Only the user raises a grant or the endpoint, in a terminal outside the agent
  host (`workit grant set <ws> defaultEndpoint=merged`); never edit
  workspaces.json or route around grant_required. Release: `workit release
  start <v>`, commits, `finish`; `publish` if asked.
- Ask only for a product or preference choice, or for authority you lack, with
  your recommended answer. Facts are yours: read, run or prototype.
- Label claims measured (run and seen this session), inferred, or guess.
  Prose is a note: only a configured check the CLI ran (`workit check <name>`)
  satisfies a gate; an ad-hoc `workit check -- <cmd>` never does.
- Author is not verifier: your own verdict is `--self`, shown as
  self-reviewed, never verified. High risk, a focused or full lane and
  merge under `verification: self|independent` need a verifier with its
  own host-derived session (a subagent's `<lead>:<child>`); never hand-mint one (`<lead>-v1`).
- A local-commit endpoint does not imply PR readiness, and a local commit alone
  is not evidence of a requested remote push. Before reporting delivery,
  reconcile every requested item and observe it (`workit verify-delivery`).

Read-only git and gh run raw; mutations go through workit verbs
(`workit git|pr|ci|check|help`; else `npx -y @workit-dev/cli`).

and a solo edit needs no task. A decision records a user choice; it never
authorizes an effect. Judge work once with

Across repositories, bind items to checkout, branch and endpoint, resolve
competing targets before a mutation, and reconcile an uncertain
effect before a retry.

Mid-task: never silently drop or resume an objective (workit-continue).

Skills: load the skill, never act from memory (aliases /wk-<name>).

- review, blast radius: workit-review
- bug, broken, flaky, regression: workit-debug

- BDD, TDD, acceptance criteria, Given/When/Then: workit-bdd
- test audit, tautology, weak tests: workit-test-audit
- deslop, slop, dead code: workit-deslop
- fan out, parallelize, parallel agents, swarm: workit-fanout
- verify the app, smoke test, prove it works: workit-verify-app
- retro (user-invoked; offer it): workit-retro
- architecture, deepen modules (user-invoked; offer it): workit-architecture
Agent spawn model/effort (pass them, workers with run_in_background: true): workit:implementer hard opus, standard sonnet, mundane haiku, workit:verifier sonnet, workit:reviewer opus, Explore haiku, ROLE: decider fable/high, ROLE: babysit haiku. Run workit verbs with the `workit` CLI on the Bash tool (`workit --help`); run `workit ci wait` in the background. Base directory for this skill: <workit>/packages/workit-claude-code/skills/implement

# Implement and prove it works

## Steps

1. Read before writing: the files you will touch, their callers, and one
   neighbour that already does something similar. Copy its patterns, names and
   error handling. Repo rules (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, lint config) win.
2. On the default branch? Branch first: `workit git branch --kind feature --slug <s>` (host note: a Claude Code host-isolated worktree uses plain `git switch -c`).
   Tracking it? Judge once: `workit policy assess --judge risk=normal behavior=yes
   product-choice=no plan=no` (trivial and no for a mechanical fix). Already
   judged? Cite the plan with `--ref <path>` or record the decision; don't re-judge.
3. Small steps that each leave the tree green. Behavior change: write the
   acceptance as Given/When/Then and see a test fail first (call the Skill tool with `workit:bdd`).
   Mechanical change: the existing checks are enough. A codemod or schematic
   goes one area at a time: run it on one directory, `workit check`, commit
   that directory, then the next; never loop it over all areas. No tautological tests:
   a test must fail if the behavior breaks, never restate the implementation.
4. Run the real checks, local-first: the targeted test or check for the file
   you touched while you work, then the full configured set once at the end
   (`workit check test`, plus `lint` and `typecheck` when the repo has them).
   Heavy work runs under one machine-wide lease: an ad-hoc
   suite is `workit check --heavy -- <cmd>`, never a hand-made flock; a busy
   lease waits and names its holder (`workit lock status`). A tool warning is a finding: fix it in this PR, or record the false positive with evidence; pre-existing ones get their own PR.
5. Prove the feature on its real surface with the project's `verify-<app>`
   skill; none yet? Write one (call the Skill tool with `workit:verify-app`). Tests show branch behavior,
   not that the feature works. The report carries what you observed: a UI
   change a screenshot or console/network check (chrome devtools or
   agent-browser), an API a quoted real response. App not runnable? Say so
   plainly, never claim success.
6. Commit: `workit git commit -m "<type>: <what>" -- <paths>`; Co-Authored-By goes in with `--trailer "Co-Authored-By: <name> <email>"`. Host note: a Workit worktree (`workit fanout worktree create`) takes `workit git --cwd <worktree> …`; a Claude Code host-isolated one (`.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>`) takes plain git (its SubagentStart text: isolation refuses a git wrapper). One file holding two changes: stage one change's hunks with `workit git stage --patch <file>` (a `git diff -- <file>` cut to them), then `workit git commit -m "<msg>" --staged` (exactly the index); a path staged in part commits only its staged hunks (`--whole` takes the file).
   No endpoint named? Stop here and state the next command. Hand delivery to
   ship, which pushes and opens the PR with its body shape (call the Skill tool with `workit:ship`), only
   when that was requested, or the request implies delivery and the effective
   endpoint in `workit grant show` is `pr`, `green` or `merged`; `green` and
   `merged` keep babysitting. Otherwise it is `commit`.
7. Verify as far as the review lane asks (`workit policy assess`, `workit pr
   status`). Lane none: no verdict. Lane self: after `workit check test` passes,
   record `workit ledger verdict tests-verified --self --how "<what you ran>"`;
   it reads self-reviewed, never verified, and is enough. Focused, full, high
   risk or `verification: self|independent` merges: one fresh verifier per PR after the last push, its own host-derived session (Claude Code: the `verifier` agent with the `model` (and `effort`) of `workit models show --role verifier`; Codex:
   the `verifier` agent; OpenCode: a child session; Pi: a supervised worker),
   never a hand-minted id. Before saying done, reconcile
   every named deliverable against the target checkout and observe it (for a push:
   `workit verify-delivery push`).

Independent slices that could run in parallel: fan them out (call the Skill tool with `workit:fanout`).
One `implementer` slice: `workit fanout worktree create <slice>` before spawning,
then `workit fanout brief <slice>`; no host isolation (Workit's hooks confine it).

Stay inline by default (workspace `delegation: inline-first`). Hand work off
only past the thresholds: an explorer after about 3 tool calls or 10k tokens
of searching, parallel writers for 2 or more disjoint units of about 100+
lines each.

## Example

Bad: "Done - added the --since flag, tests pass." (no check ran this turn; the
flag was never invoked)

Good: "Added `--since`. measured: `workit check test` exit 0;
`mytool log --since 2d` printed 3 entries against the fixture repo. inferred:
the GitLab path behaves the same (not run). Handed to the verifier agent."

## Check

```sh
workit check test   # then, when the endpoint was a push or beyond: workit verify-delivery push
```

feature/logger
#!/bin/sh
# Rewrites oldLog to log in every .ts file of one directory.
set -e
[ -d "$1" ] || { echo "usage: sh scripts/codemod.sh <dir>" >&2; exit 2; }
for f in "$1"/*.ts; do sed -i.bak 's/oldLog/log/g' "$f" && rm -f "$f.bak"; done
echo "codemod: rewrote $1"
src/billing:
invoice.ts

src/orders:
order.ts

src/users:
user.ts

README.md
scripts
src
.workit
workit check: Run a configured or ad-hoc check and record CLI-observed evidence (exit = the command's); heavy checks wait for the machine-wide heavy-check lease

usage: workit check <name> [--full] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--wait <dur> | --no-wait] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] | workit check [--name <n>] [--shell] [--full] [--timeout <s>] [--task <id>] [--base <ref>] [--heavy [--wait <dur> | --no-wait]] [--no-lease --reason "<why>"] -- <cmd…>

The heavy-check lease: heavy work (tests, builds, installs, image builds) shares one machine-wide lease, so parallel agents and worktrees never exhaust this machine's memory and CPU. `slots` (default 1) heavy checks run at once; on Linux each also runs in a systemd scope with MemoryMax and CPUQuota.

Queueing: a heavy check that finds every slot held joins a first-come, first-served queue and prints `waiting for the heavy-check lease` naming the holder (check, pid, session, age, directory) and its position, then a status line every 30 s. It waits `--wait <dur>` (90, 90s, 30m, 1h), else `resources.wait` (default 30 min), and exits 4 (busy) only past that wait or at once with --no-wait. A waiter that is killed gives up its place. A wait longer than your shell tool's timeout belongs in a background call. `workit lock status` shows the holders and the queue.

Light checks: the named checks lint, typecheck and format (`resources.light`, set in workspaces.json) never take the lease, so they run at once beside a long suite.

--heavy: an ad-hoc `workit check -- <cmd>` takes the lease only with --heavy; the named checks test and build always do. The shell hook runs a raw heavy command (`npx jest`, `npm run test:ci`, `cargo test`, `docker build`) as `workit check --heavy -- <cmd>` on Claude Code, OpenCode and Pi, and denies it with that exact command on Codex and Cursor.

--no-lease skips the lease and needs --reason "<why>". Never hand-roll a flock: the lease already queues every agent on the machine.

Output: a check prints the last 60 lines of its output and one summary line with `log: <path>` to the full log; --full streams all of it.

examples:
  workit check test
  workit check --heavy -- npx jest
  workit check test --wait 45m
  workit check --name unit -- bun test test/unit
  workit check test --no-lease --reason "machine is idle, debugging a hang"

A value that starts with - goes as --flag=value (or after a bare --).

content.text:
The codemod ran on `src/billing`, `src/orders` and `src/users`, one directory at a time, and each area is its own commit on `feature/logger`. The tree is clean.

- `c631609` refactor: migrate billing to log
- `dfe56c8` refactor: migrate orders to log
- `9aee7a5` refactor: migrate users to log

Each commit has the Co-Authored-By trailer for Claude Haiku 5.5.

**Checks (measured):** `workit check test` passed, exit 0, after each area. Afterwards, `grep oldLog src/` finds only the `export const oldLog = log;` line in `src/log.ts`, which the codemod doesn't touch by design.

**Limits:**
- The configured `test` check is a grep that confirms each `src/*/*.ts` file has an `import { log }` or `import { oldLog }` line. It would still pass if a call site were broken, so it is weak evidence for this change. It is the only check configured, so I did not run lint or typecheck.
- I did not run the app or verify on a real surface. This is a mechanical rename, so the existing checks were the bar the skill sets.
- No endpoint was named, so I stopped at the local commits. The branch is not pushed and no PR is open. Next step if you want it delivered: `workit:ship` to push and open the PR.
- The `oldLog` alias in `src/log.ts` is still there. Removing it is a separate follow-up once nothing else uses it.
